protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Unknown: no row measures µs-ms exchange in the free truncated APOBEC2 (41-224) that matches the entry; its only relaxation data (700 MHz, 25 °C, pH 7.0, zinc bound) are reported in readable text only as an overall tumbling time of 17 ns, and the amides missing from its spectra at 37 °C have no established mechanism.
protein_summary.deposition_readback: Deposition-derived; same numbers RelaxDB labels were computed from; not literature confirmation. BMRB 18306 holds 700 MHz T1 and T2 for 108 residues and NOE for 152, with metadata pH 7.0, 50 mM ionic strength and 310 K, while the paper's relaxation methods give 25 °C; no source names the accession. Median R2/R1 over NOE >= 0.65 residues is 41.6, which the paper's formula turns into about 17.5 ns, matching its 17 ns. NOE below 0.65 flags 41 residues, mostly I4-L10, G44-A48 and E158-Q166 (author 41-47, 81-85 and 195-203) plus scattered sites; R2/R1 above 54.2 flags Y52, C94 and I141 (author Y89, C131 and I178), and C131 is a named active-site landmark.
open_conflicts: Temperature of the relaxation set: the paper's methods give 25 °C for the 700 MHz relaxation, BMRB 18306 metadata gives 310 K (r1, deposition readback).
questions_for_gina: Is BMRB 18306 the 700 MHz relaxation set of this paper, and which temperature is right, the paper's 25 °C or the deposited 310 K?
Is it worth retrieving Figure S1 (per-residue R1/R2/NOE) so the ps-ns profile and the deposited R2/R1 outliers at Y89, C131 and I178 can be judged from literature?
protein_summary.buffer_note: All APOBEC2 samples use A2 buffer (20 mM HEPES, 50 mM NaCl, 5 mM DTT, pH 7.0) with zinc bound. The entry construct is the truncated A2 (41-224); it precipitates during long measurements at 37 °C, so 37 °C missing-peak and assignment data describe only the soluble fraction and are kept apart from the 25 °C relaxation and SEC-MALS data. Assignment spectra used 1 mM triple-labelled (2H,13C,15N) protein. Full-length A2 (1-224) rows are another construct. Second read flagged no row.
